tour.title: EA600 East Anglia Road Trip
tour.summary: Escape the motorways and discover a slower, more beautiful side of England on the EA600 — a spectacular circular road trip through the timeless landscapes, coastlines and hidden treasures of East Anglia.
tour.description: The EA600 traces a circle from Cambridge through the fens, along the whole of the Norfolk and Suffolk coast, and home through medieval wool towns — on quiet A and B roads built for slow driving.

stops.title: Cambridge
stops.description: College spires, the Backs and the start line.

stops.title: Ely
stops.description: The 'Ship of the Fens' rising over flat black earth.

stops.title: King's Lynn
stops.description: Medieval merchant quays on the Great Ouse.

stops.title: Hunstanton
stops.description: Striped cliffs and sunsets over the Wash.

stops.title: Wells-next-the-Sea
stops.description: Harbour town, Holkham sands and pinewoods.

stops.title: Cromer
stops.description: Victorian pier, crab shacks and clifftop air.

stops.title: Norwich
stops.description: Cathedral city on the edge of the Broads.

stops.title: Great Yarmouth
stops.description: Golden mile, seals and wide eastern skies.

stops.title: Southwold
stops.description: Lighthouse, beach huts and Adnams ale.

stops.title: Aldeburgh
stops.description: Shingle, fishing boats and Britten's scallop.

stops.title: Woodbridge
stops.description: Tide mill, river Deben and Sutton Hoo.

days.tip: Stop at Wicken Fen for the reed beds at dusk.

highlights.title: Scenic Drives
highlights.description: Winding country roads, vast skies and unforgettable views at every turn.

highlights.title: Rich History
highlights.description: Castles, cathedral cities, medieval towns and England's fascinating heritage.

highlights.title: Coastal Beauty
highlights.description: Sandy beaches, estuaries, hidden harbours and charming seaside towns.

highlights.title: Hidden Gems
highlights.description: Villages, marshes and secret places waiting to be explored.

destinations.title: Norwich
destinations.description: A Norman cathedral, cobbled lanes and the gateway to the Broads.

destinations.title: Cromer
destinations.description: Pier-end sunsets and the famous sweet Cromer crab.

destinations.title: Holkham
destinations.description: Four miles of empty sand backed by Corsican pines — the finest beach in England.

destinations.title: Lavenham
destinations.description: Crooked timber-framed houses built on medieval wool fortunes.

destinations.title: Southwold
destinations.description: A white lighthouse standing guard over pastel cottages, beach huts and a pier that still feels like 1938.

planning_tips.title: When to Go
planning_tips.description: May through September is ideal for long evenings and open attractions. Spring and autumn are quieter on the roads.

planning_tips.title: Where to Stay
planning_tips.description: Coaching inns, harbour cottages and country-house hotels in each overnight town.

planning_tips.title: Driving Information
planning_tips.description: Mostly A and B roads with single-track coastal lanes. Drive on the left.

planning_tips.title: Parking
planning_tips.description: Pay-and-display in most towns. National Trust members park free at many sites.

planning_tips.title: Food & Dining
planning_tips.description: Cromer crab, Brancaster mussels, Adnams ale and proper Sunday roasts.

planning_tips.title: What to Pack
planning_tips.description: Layers for coastal wind, walking boots and something for the beach.

planning_tips.title: Useful Information
planning_tips.description: Emergency 999. Many village shops close early and on Sundays.

planning_tips.title: Trip Duration
planning_tips.description: Seven days is ideal. Five is possible; ten lets you slow right down.

questions.question: How long does the full route take?
questions.answer: Most travelers take 5 to 7 days, but the route can flex from a long weekend to two relaxed weeks.

questions.question: What's the best season to drive it?
questions.answer: May through September offers the longest days; spring and autumn are quieter.

questions.question: Are there EV charging stops along the way?
questions.answer: Major towns on the loop have public chargers — plan overnight stops in advance.

questions.question: What type of car can I bring?
questions.answer: Any comfortable car works; narrow coastal lanes reward a smaller footprint.

questions.question: Can I drive the route in sections?
questions.answer: Yes — the EA600 works as day trips or multi-day stages from Cambridge or Norwich.
